# canlang v1 design

Status: chosen language design, October 3, 2026. This specifies a compiler/runtime to implement; it does not claim either exists. [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) owns the product goals. This document resolves their syntax and semantics. [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) retains the history and identifies superseded draft choices.

The target is a company business application: records, permissions, rules, workflows, and a standard browser/MCP interface. An app does not implement authentication, retries, HTML widgets, or database coordination itself. Unknown words never install imagined business behavior. Adoption and dependable generation take precedence over preserving ambiguous draft shorthand.

## 1. Source and composition

Source is UTF-8. Identifiers match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, are case-sensitive, and use `.` for qualification. Two spaces form an indentation level; tabs are errors. Newlines end statements outside `()`, `[]`, and `{}`. A semicolon separates simple statements; compound statements require an indented block. Strings use JSON double-quoted syntax. There is no string interpolation: use typed formatting expressions. Keywords are contextual, so a field may be named `from` or `end`.

`#` at the start of a source line attaches description metadata to the next declaration at the same indentation. Consecutive lines join with a newline. `##` is recognized first and is an ordinary ignored comment. Blank lines or `##` between a description and declaration do not change attachment. An unattached description is an error. `description=` is not declaration metadata. Business fields named `description` are ordinary data.

The app description is required. Descriptions apply uniformly to packages, models, fields, operations, pages, capabilities, and other declarations. Multiline field declarations permit field descriptions. Standard CRUD descriptions are generated; custom user-callable scenarios require a description explaining their business effect. Internal handlers may have descriptions, but none become executable behavior.

A build takes an explicit set of `.can` files, containing exactly one `app` declaration. Files have no namespaces, imports, initialization order, or runtime effects. No scanning ancestor directories or automatically importing every neighboring file.

Small-app form:

```can
# Track the team's work.
app Tasks
Given
  runtime workerd
  database D1
  auth email password
  teams
  Todo in team { title:text! trim, done:bool=false }
  policy Todo read=members
When
  crud Todo by=members fields=title,done
Then
  page / title="Tasks"
    form Todo.create display=inline
    list Todo
      edit
      delete
```

This is package `main`. Its Given contains shared context and its own declarations. Explicit-package form moves shared context into `context`:

```can
# Manage customers and their work.
app Office
context
  runtime workerd
  database D1
  auth email password
  teams
package crm
  Given
    Customer in team { name:text! }
    policy Customer read=members
  When
    crud Customer by=members fields=name
  Then
    page /customers title="Customers"
      list Customer
        edit
package work
  use crm.Customer
  Given
    Task in team { customer:Customer!, title:text! }
    policy Task read=members
  When
    crud Task by=members fields=customer,title
  Then
    page /tasks title="Tasks"
      list Task
```

Each package has exactly one ordered Given/When/Then structure; sections may be empty. A package block belongs to one source location and can move between files without changing meaning. Multiple packages can occupy one file. The implicit and explicit forms cannot be mixed. `context` permits runtime, database, auth, teams, theme, bindings, services, and adapters; no business models or operations.

`use package.Name` imports one declaration, giving its local final name; `use package.Name as Alias` resolves collisions. No wildcard imports. Without a `use`, a cross-package reference is an error, including a qualified reference. Shared context has no owning package and refers to declarations by their fully qualified names, for example `key=booking.Calendar`. An import grants name visibility, never data access. Types and operations have stable `package.Name` identities; generated CRUD lives under `package.Model.operation`. Dependency cycles between stored model references are allowed; containment, derived-value, hook, and synchronous call cycles are errors. A model, its policies, its invariants, and its canonical CRUD belong to one package. Other packages can call its declared operations, but cannot directly mutate it or extend its policy.

## 2. Data and types

`Model in team {fields}` stores a team-scoped model. `Model in Parent {fields}` creates a child with an implicit required, immutable `parent:Parent`; it inherits the parent's team and storage owner. `Model in app` is app-scoped and requires explicit policies. No omitted ownership. A child is accessed as `parentRecord.Child`; that is a typed collection, not a copied relation. Other relationships are explicit model-typed fields. Changing containment or team is not an ordinary update.

Every record has `id`, `version`, `created`, `updated`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, and nullable `archived_at`. These names are reserved. IDs are opaque strings; attribution names stable accounts or trusted sources and survives membership removal. A model name denotes a type/collection, **never a current record**.

| Type | Value and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `bool`, `int`, `decimal` | Unicode string, boolean, signed 64-bit integer, exact decimal with at most 38 significant digits and 18 fractional digits; overflow is an error |
| `enum(a,b,...)` | Closed set of identifier values, serialized as strings |
| `email`, `url` | Validated strings; URLs limited to HTTP(S); email verification belongs to auth |
| `date`, `datetime`, `duration`, `timezone` | Calendar date; UTC instant; integer milliseconds; IANA zone identifier |
| `currency`, `money` | ISO currency code; `{minor:int,currency:currency}` with pinned currency minor-unit scales |
| `user`, `member` | Stable account reference; team-scoped membership reference with retained attribution |
| `Model`, `Model.field` | Record reference; reuse a field's value type and validation constraints |
| `Contract` | Named structural value, stored by value, not a live model reference |
| `file`, `secret`, `json` | Completed immutable R2 reference; server-only opaque secret; opaque bounded JSON |
| `T[]`, `T?`, `A\|B` | Homogeneous ordered array, nullable value, tagged union of named types |

`contract Address {street:text!,city:text!}` defines a structural type. Contract fields follow model field rules but have no ownership or metadata. JSON has no arbitrary property access. `if value is Contract` validates a JSON value against that closed contract (including bounds, defaults, and rejection of unknown fields), and narrows it within the true branch; failure takes the false branch. A union's wire value is `{type:"QualifiedType",value:...}`; common compatible fields are readable, and `if value is Type` narrows a branch. A model reference is not an embedded copy of its record.

Stored field forms are deliberately distinct:

- `name:T!` requires a non-null create value.
- `name:T?` defaults to null; explicit null is legal.
- `name:T=expr` supplies a non-null default on creation only.
- `name:T[]` defaults to `[]`; `T[]!` requires an array input.
- `name:T server=expr` supplies the server value on creation and excludes it from client inputs. `secret` fields always require server initialization.

An unmarked scalar without a default/server expression is an error. Field modifiers are `trim`, `min=`, `max=`, and `unique`; text/array min/max measure length, numeric min/max measure value, and bounds are inclusive. Constraints run after normalization. Explicit `require` handles strict inequalities and relationships. `unique Model fields=a,b [where=expr]` declares a composite uniqueness constraint within its containing parent, team, or app. Null values do not participate unless the predicate explicitly includes them. Retained archived rows participate.

`derive Model.field:T = expr` defines a read-only computed field in scope `row:Model`. `derive name(p:T,...):R = expr` defines a pure function. Parameters and result types are explicit; obvious local values and generated CRUD schemas are inferred. Field type references remove repeated enum/bound definitions. Derived definitions cannot recurse, perform effects, or depend on incidental UI state.

Reference examples use only declared domain fields. There are no magical `predicate`, `time_ranges`, `immutable_amount`, or provider-controlled field types. Represent business structures with contracts and canonical rules.

## 3. Expressions, queries, and scopes

An expression is a literal, lexical name, field access, list/struct value, typed function call, query, or operator expression. Struct literals use `{field=expr}`; `{field}` means `{field=field}`. A contract value is `Address {street,city}`. Operators from lowest to highest precedence: `or`, `and`, prefix `not`, comparisons (`== != < <= > >= in is`), `+ -`, `* / %`, unary `-`, member access/call/index. Boolean operators short-circuit. Chained comparisons are forbidden. No implicit truthiness, string/number coercion, assignment expression, or arbitrary JavaScript.

Null equals null; other ordered/arithmetic operations on null are type errors unless narrowed by a preceding check. `coalesce(value,fallback)` removes null. Enum literals require a uniquely expected enum type. Unresolved bare identifiers are errors. Indexing arrays uses zero-based integers and `at(array,index)` returns a nullable item; no unchecked `[]` indexing. Currency values never coerce to decimal.

Lexical names are parameters, `let` values, query aliases, imported declarations, and fixed context: `actor:user?`, `team:Team` when applicable, `now:datetime`, and `operation:OperationContext` with read-only `id:text` and `source:text` fields. Team exposes `id` and `timezone`; a membership exposes `id`, `user:user`, and `team:Team`. Authenticated/member/role authorization narrows actor to non-null. Trusted handlers have `actor=null`; attribution uses their verified source, and team is derived from the verified occurrence, never an arbitrary payload grant. `now` is fixed at admission across internal retries; generated IDs and random values are also stable across retries. `row` is bound only inside a model policy/invariant/derive/lock or a collection child; scenario bodies use their named record parameters. Bare field selectors in UI attributes such as `columns=title,done` are schema selectors, not general expressions. There is no fallback search through unrelated records for a matching field.

Queries have one form, starting from a model, parent-child collection, array, or typed collection-valued local:

```can
Model as item where predicate order=-item.created select expression
invoice.Line as line select line.quantity*line.price
```

`where`, `order`, and `select` are optional and ordered as shown. An omitted select yields records. Aliases are required when an expression accesses an element. Query values can feed `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `any`, `all`, `first`, or a presentation collection. `any(domain as x,predicate)` and `all(domain as x,predicate)` separate the domain from the predicate. `all` of an empty domain is true; `any` is false. Require `count(domain)>0` separately where necessary. `first` returns nullable and requires stable ordering. `min`/`max` of an empty domain are null; numeric sum is zero; money sum requires an explicit currency when the domain may be empty: `sum(query,currency)`.

Default record queries exclude archived rows. `Model archived=include` explicitly includes them. Record ordering defaults to `created,id`; ID is appended as a final tie-breaker. `group(query as item,keyExpr)` binds that alias in its key expression and produces typed `{key,items}` groups, usable in queries and reports. For example, `group(selected as expense,expense.status)`. It never invents fields or a callable function from a group name.

Pure builtins are closed and typed: `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `any`, `all`, `first`, `group`, `at`, `coalesce`, `abs`, `round(value,scale)`, `lower`, `upper`, `trim`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `join`, `format`, `active_member`, `overlaps`, `local_date`, `local_instant`, `add_days`, and `money`, `date`, `datetime`, and `random_secret`. Their meanings are ordinary typed operations, with these important boundaries:

- `format(template,values)` uses named `{key}` substitutions, escapes for the output context, and cannot execute code. No arbitrary formatter plugins.
- `overlaps(aStart,aEnd,bStart,bEnd)` tests non-empty half-open ranges. Date arithmetic uses `add_days`; a duration added to a datetime is elapsed time, not local calendar time.
- `local_instant(date,time,zone,fold)` requires `fold=earlier` or `later` for an ambiguous local time; nonexistent local times fail. `time` is a validated `HH:MM[:SS]` string here.
- Decimal rounding and money multiplication/division use half-even. `money(decimal,currency)` rounds once to that currency's minor units. Add/subtract/compare money only with matching currencies. Currency conversion requires an explicit typed provider/result workflow.
- `active_member(member,team)` checks current membership; it is not a history-visibility predicate.
- `date("YYYY-MM-DD")` and `datetime("RFC3339 instant")` are checked constructors. Source duration literals are integers suffixed `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, or `d` (a day is exactly 24 hours); byte literals use `B`, `KiB`, `MiB`, or `GiB`. Overflow fails. Quotas and recurring intervals must be positive.
- `random_secret()` produces 32 cryptographically random bytes represented as an opaque secret. It is permitted only in server defaults, is never client-readable, and reuses the same value for the same committed operation identity.

Function signatures and argument counts are checked; a convenient function name never supplies an undeclared implementation. Large queries may use SQL aggregates; runtime limits must reject an oversized invariant calculation, never calculate it over a truncated page.

## 4. Permissions and rules

`auth email password` provides verified-email registration, sign-in/out, expiring email-token recovery, sessions, and MCP authorization. `teams` adds owner-managed membership, expiring verified-email invitations, roles, team selection, and a team timezone (UTC until configured). Deployment provisions the first owner. `role billing in=team` declares an owner-assigned role; `owner` and `members` are built in. App authors do not implement alternative login or role tables.

`members`, `owner`, a declared role, `authenticated`, and `public` are actor predicates. They can combine with boolean record predicates. At team scope they test the resolved team. `actor` is null for public requests. A completed membership removal prevents new admissions; an already admitted operation may finish. On D1 the fenced commit also detects intervening membership changes. Historic membership references remain readable where record policies permit; new member assignments must be active.

```can
policy Candidate read=recruiter
policy Candidate read=interviewer where=row.interviewer!=null and row.interviewer.user==actor fields=name,interview_at
require Line: row.quantity>0
lock Invoice fields=customer,total when=row.status!=draft
```

Policies grant **reads**, including files. No policy means deny. Matching grants union their fields for matching rows; omitted `fields` grants ordinary fields and safe record metadata, never secrets. Identity/team/parent boundaries always apply. Public and external-user grants are explicit exceptions to membership requirements, evaluated in the resolved record/team scope. New cross-team record relationships are rejected.

User queries apply row/field permissions before filters, searches, ordering, counts, aggregates, relationship expansion, and serialization. A derived value is readable only if its data dependencies are readable. A confidential aggregate needs a specifically authorized read scenario with `scope=authority`, described below. No separate `projection` primitive duplicates policy field grants.

`require Model: predicate` is a pure invariant in `row` scope, checked for every affected row in the proposed final state. Dependency analysis rechecks relevant rows when referenced data changes; oversized dependency work fails with a bounded-work error. Deleting a referenced row fails unless references have been removed in the same operation. Invariants do not emit events or perform effects.

`lock Model fields=... when=predicate` evaluates on the **pre-state**. If true, those field values cannot change and the row cannot be removed, including through scenarios or hooks. The transition establishing the lock may set final values. A child rule may inspect `row.parent`. Archival preserves locked values. No separate freeze/immutable/snapshot variants: copy selected values into typed snapshot fields with `set`/`create`, then lock them. Audit history is automatic.

Operation `by` governs its writes independently of generic CRUD input fields. All paths still enforce ownership, invariants, locks, versions, and reference validity. Scenarios may inspect authority data needed for their rules; this does not grant callers access to that data. Guard failures default to a generic business-rule error; custom literal messages must not interpolate confidential values.

## 5. Canonical operations

```can
crud Todo by=members fields=title,done,assignee delete=archive
# Complete an open task.
scenario complete(todo:Todo) by=members
  require not todo.done
  then set todo {done=true}
```

There is at most one `crud` declaration per model. It generates create, update, and delete operations. `fields` is the update allowlist and, unless `create_fields` is supplied, the create allowlist. `create=none`, `update=none`, or `delete=none` disables that operation. `when=predicate` applies to each proposed create/update row and the existing delete row; mandatory cross-path business rules belong in invariants/locks. All required create fields must be supplied, defaulted, or server-owned. A child create takes its protected parent binding. Create defaults do not run again on update; omitted update fields are unchanged, and explicit null clears a nullable field.

`delete=archive` is the default: delete archives the row and its contained subtree, atomically. It does not create a second archive API. `delete=remove` permanently removes an unreferenced row/subtree and is explicit. Existing references to archived rows remain valid for authorized history; new references cannot target them. Archived rows cannot be edited; restoration is outside v1. Audit/receipt retention is independent of deletion.

A scenario declares every parameter's type. `p:T` is required; `p:T?` defaults to null; `p:T=expr` has a default. `Model.field` inherits value constraints, not its storage default/server ownership. There is no inference from parameter spelling or later prose. Parameter defaults are pure and evaluated at invocation. A mutation's record parameters carry expected versions; read parameters need only IDs.

The effect vocabulary is finite:

| Statement | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `let name=expr` | Immutable local binding |
| `require expr [message="literal"]` | Reject without committing if false |
| `create Model {fields} as name` | Insert and bind a record; child inputs include `parent` |
| `set record {fields}` | Assign named fields; no implied copies or model-name rebinding |
| `delete record` | Apply the model's declared deletion mode; allowed only if deletion is enabled |
| `call operation {arguments} [as name]` | Invoke a canonical operation in the same transaction/context; recheck its `by`, rules and ownership |
| `if expr` / `else` | Indented conditional branches |
| `for item in query limit=N` | Bounded loop; fail the entire operation if more than N items would be processed |
| `emit Event {fields}` | Persist one typed domain event for post-commit handling |
| `send Target.operation {arguments} [when=predicate] as delivery` | Persist a typed external delivery intent; returns a receipt, not provider success |
| `schedule key at=instant event=Event {fields}` | Replace one named pending occurrence at this owner; key is a text expression |
| `cancel key` | Cancel the named pending occurrence if not dispatched |
| `return expr` | Return one statically typed result and end evaluation |

One inline `then` may contain simple statements separated by `;`; a block `then` contains any statements. No nested `atomic`: a mutation is already one atomic unit at its inferred owner. No `clear`, `insert`, `upsert`, `append`, `snapshot`, `freeze`, arbitrary SQL/JS, or free-form effects. Collections stored by value are replaced through `set`; large mutable child collections are models.

Cross-package `call` is the only way to mutate another package's model. It participates in the caller's operation identity, invokes no network request, and cannot recurse. Direct parameter assignment is never storage mutation. A scenario cannot synthesize user privilege or trusted source status.

Mutation results default to a receipt plus authorized changed-record projections. Explicit mutation returns may contain literals, input values, generated receipts, and readable record values. Private authority-derived scalars cannot leak through return values; the compiler tracks these dependencies. A deliberate privileged report uses `scenario ... read=true scope=authority -> Contract by=...`: its typed result is an explicit information grant to `by`. Ordinary `read=true` uses viewer queries, allows only pure statements, and has a required result type and return on every path. Source-scoped reports must have a description identifying the information exposed. Mutation success/failure can inherently reveal the stated operation's permitted business outcome, such as availability; it never returns hidden rows or SQL diagnostics.

## 6. Handlers and events

`by=` means a user-callable operation. `on=` means a typed trusted source. They are mutually exclusive. Handler input is inferred from that source and bound to `event`; handlers declare no client parameters and never become MCP tools. `scenario name on=Source` retains the same require/then body.

| Source | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `Model.create`, `.update`, `.delete` | Pre-commit CRUD hook; `event.before`, `event.after`, and `event.input` have generated types; unavailable record side is null |
| `Model.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted` | Committed change event with record ID, owner, resulting version, and occurrence ID |
| `teams.member_removed` | Committed team/membership IDs and retained account attribution |
| Declared `Event` | Payload from `event Event {fields}` and `emit`/`schedule` |
| `every(5m)` | Runtime tick with scheduled and actual instants |
| Named queue or adapter event | Payload from its declared contract, verified by its ingress |

At most one hook per model/CRUD operation. Hooks run on the proposed state before invariants/locks/commit, can reject or adjust it, and cannot introduce new client parameters. On create, event.before is null; on update both record sides exist; on archive-delete after is the archived record, and on remove-delete it is null. Before/input are read-only. `set event.after {fields}` adjusts the pending create/update record without recursively invoking CRUD; a delete hook can reject but cannot adjust its target. They cannot call back into the triggering CRUD. Scenario effects also emit committed model-change events; they do not pretend to be CRUD or re-run CRUD hooks. Rules that must apply to all writes therefore belong in Given invariants/locks. A committed event handler is a later transaction; it cannot retroactively reject its source operation.

Committed-event payloads are immutable identities, not an implicit historical record snapshot. Loading their record reads current authority state; obsolete work must check current guards. Declare event payload fields for values that must be preserved at emission. Each handler receives an independent stable occurrence identity, and duplicate deliveries replay its receipt. Do not infer events from enum names or scenario names.

Recurring `every(duration)` ticks are UTC-epoch aligned; missed periods coalesce to one current occurrence. Calendar-specific schedules compute an explicit `at` instant. A dynamic schedule key is unique within app/owner/package, independent of the calling operation, so booking, rescheduling, and cancellation can address the same key. Cross-package changes call the owning package's operation. Replacement and cancellation commit with business changes. Handler guards run again when due. Replacing a pending occurrence supersedes it; already admitted work or provider-accepted messages may complete. A superseded/cancelled occurrence also supersedes its undispatched delivery intents. A send's optional `when` is a pure dispatch guard over current owner state and retained lexical inputs; omitting it means unconditional delivery of that committed event. State-dependent notices declare that guard. Dispatch atomically checks supersession and the guard before claiming the provider call; false means skipped. Business-operation admission guards are not implicitly rerun after their effects. Persist pending, delivered, failed, and uncertain outcomes. A handler's false guard completes it as skipped; a transient runtime failure retries the same occurrence.

Email is `send Mail.send` through the standard email contract, inside a business or event-handler scenario. It is not a second free-form workflow language under Then. Then is exclusively presentation; earlier standalone `email ...` draft lines migrate to typed handlers. Notification content, recipient, and schedule are business choices; delivery bookkeeping is runtime behavior.

## 7. Storage, consistency, and retries

Every mutation has one authoritative storage owner. D1 is the default. A first-class binding can move a whole related group:

```can
binding Schedule DurableObject key=Calendar
Calendar in team at=Schedule { name:text! }
Booking in Calendar { start:datetime!, end:datetime! }
require Booking: row.start<row.end
```

Each Calendar ID selects one SQLite Durable Object instance; its children inherit it. New root IDs derive deterministically from the complete operation identity, including the originating principal/team/operation, so a fresh replay routes to the same owner. Child references include their root routing identity. The runtime supplies a root-ID/owner directory and authorization context, not a writable D1 duplicate of those records. The directory is an eventual discovery index updated through committed owner work; it never decides record access or availability. A returned root ID routes directly even before indexing completes. Team-scoped browsing of roots uses that directory and loads authorized owner records with bounded fan-out. Cross-owner joins/aggregates are forbidden in business mutations; read views are explicitly eventual. A reference can identify another owner but cannot imply an atomic read or write there. Invariants must live entirely within one owner. Cross-owner workflows use durable events and explicit pending business state. Atomic owner transfers are outside v1.

CRUD and scenarios infer their authority from mutated records and dependencies. A call targeting more than one owner instance fails before commit. Pure shared constants are allowed; mutable remote configuration needed for a decision must be copied into authoritative state with declared version semantics. No per-scenario authority selectors, user-written reservation mirrors, or pretend transactions across services.

D1 does not provide a JavaScript transaction callback for arbitrary read/branch/write workflows. V1 uses a **database-wide optimistic revision fence**:

1. Read the primary revision before all state-dependent reads, including permissions, receipts, relations, and aggregates.
2. Evaluate bounded pure DSL against those reads and proposed local changes. No externally observable effects occur.
3. In one D1 SQL batch, assert the same revision, apply writes/constraints/history/receipt/outbox, and increment the revision. The assertion must raise an SQL error on mismatch; a zero-row update is insufficient.
4. A failed assertion rolls back the entire batch and retries evaluation, at most three attempts. Submitted stale record versions still produce a conflict, not an automatic overwrite. Exhausted contention returns a retryable error.

All runtime writers participate, including membership, delivery bookkeeping, and migration writes. External raw writes invalidate the contract. Revision values never reset while admissions continue. Reads use the primary in v1. Pure read operations validate the revision again after dependent reads; changed revisions retry rather than return a mixed authorization snapshot. A successful mutation rechecks current read permission before serializing its result.

This is our proposed execution strategy based on [D1's transactional batch guarantee](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#batch), not a performance result. A prototype must establish acceptable contention/latency before claiming production readiness. Durable Objects use their local SQLite transaction semantics; workerd without provisioned bindings does not supply Cloudflare services.

Mutation envelopes include a stable UUIDv7 operation ID and expected versions for existing record inputs. The runtime generates these for browser forms; MCP exposes them as protocol inputs without `.can` boilerplate. Receipt identity includes app, owner/team, principal, fully qualified operation, and ID. Authenticate and locate/check a receipt before version checks, dynamic defaults, or business evaluation. Hash normalized explicitly supplied inputs (including their submitted versions), distinguishing omission from null; persist originally resolved defaults separately. Different reuse conflicts. Completed replay returns the saved outcome projected against current access, even though its submitted versions are now stale. A repeated request with the same identity never intentionally initiates a second external payment.

Runtime defaults: identities older than 24 hours are rejected, with five minutes of future clock tolerance; ordinary receipts remain at least seven days. First check for an existing receipt, then enforce age for an unseen identity. After receipt expiry an old identity cannot execute anew. Trusted occurrence IDs are runtime-owned and retained through the entire retry horizon. Payment identities remain associated with their payment records. Audit history defaults to 90 days; longer business evidence is declared as actual retained records. Deployment may lengthen retention, and must never shorten it below replay/retry requirements. Restores stop admissions and invalidate in-flight attempts before resuming.

Every external effect is a durable outbox item committed with its originating state. Its identity derives from operation ID, source declaration, and deterministic occurrence index. Delivery uses exponential backoff with jitter, at most eight attempts within 24 hours by default; capability contracts may require a longer reconciliation period. Permanent errors stop retries. Recovery scans find unsent work without depending on an in-memory callback. Provider uncertainty remains uncertain until reconciled; retries reuse the original provider identity. Dead-letter/failed items are visible to authorized operators.

Cloudflare Queues provide [at-least-once delivery](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/reference/delivery-guarantees/); outbox receipts and current-state guards handle duplicates and reordering. No exactly-once external delivery promise. Schedules use a shared D1 due-work dispatcher or the owner's Durable Object alarm, selected by runtime. App source declares timing, not a Cron/alarm plumbing layer.

## 8. First-class services and integrations

The v1 service registry is finite. These declarations are recognized and typed, rather than raw environment handles:

| Declaration | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `database D1` | Default authoritative relational storage and generated indexes/migrations |
| `binding Name DurableObject key=RootModel` | Per-root authority described above |
| `files R2 types="application/pdf,image/png" max=10MiB` | Bounded upload, immutable completed file references, authorized download |
| `queue Jobs type=Work` | `send Jobs.publish {value}` and `on=Jobs` typed delivery; bound Queues transport |
| `cache KV ttl=5m` | Runtime cache for explicitly public, reconstructible presentation assets/results; never permission, session, receipt, or invariant authority |
| `analytics Events {kind:text!,value:decimal!}` | `send Events.write {kind,value}` to Analytics Engine; telemetry is not authoritative billing/audit data |

Application-owned queues/telemetry have declared deployment quotas; overload records failure rather than pretending success. KV is an optional runtime optimization; no second user data CRUD API. Additional Cloudflare products can add versioned typed registry contracts when needed. Workers AI, Vectorize, Workflows, and arbitrary product SDK surfaces are not silently included in v1. These boundaries do not prevent future first-class support.

R2 uploads have a generated runtime flow: authorize intent, enforce type/size/quota, upload, finalize, attach the resulting reference. A partial upload is unusable. MIME labels alone do not validate content; supported formats are checked by runtime. Unattached uploads expire; replacing a reference never overwrites content. Attaching a file requires a finalized upload owned by the current app/team/principal, or an existing attachment the caller may read; recheck destination field limits. Possessing an opaque file ID alone grants nothing. Download is allowed through an owning record/field the caller may read, without requiring access to other owners of the same object. Links cannot grant more access than that flow. Completed but unreferenced objects are garbage-collected after the receipt/attachment horizon.

Structural `contract` defines data. `capability` defines external operations/events:

```can
contract ErrorReport { message:text!, occurred_at:datetime! }
contract ReportAccepted { reference:text! }
capability Errors version=1
  report(value:ErrorReport) -> ReportAccepted
adapter Catch capability=Errors from=deployment.Catch
```

Capability operations have typed inputs and eventual provider results. `-> R` describes that provider result, not the enqueue receipt. `event changed {fields}` inside a capability declares a verified inbound event; `on=Catch.changed` selects it. `DeliveryResult` is the runtime `{id,status}` receipt type. `send Catch.report {value}` persists work; synchronous provider results are not available inside a business transaction. Adapter completion is exposed as the typed `Catch.report.completed` source, carrying `{delivery_id,status,result:R?,error:DeliveryError?}`; success has a result, failure has a typed safe error, and uncertainty is not success. `send` itself always returns DeliveryResult.

Deployment binds an adapter to a versioned implementation of that contract. For another canlang app or a typed HTTP/service binding, the contract and explicit wire mapping are sufficient; vendor-specific authentication, signatures, pagination, and error mapping belong to that adapter implementation. The compiler checks the small declared contract, never the entire Sentry/Stripe API or the identity of CanCatch. No runtime contract discovery, version guessing, or automatic compatibility negotiation. Secrets are server-only; public intake configuration is separately declared in the capability manifest.

Standard runtime contracts cover email, payment collection/refund/reconciliation, and error reporting. They use the same adapter mechanism, not competing app syntax. Payment requests require positive money, a stable logical identity, and a persisted pending result; zero-value invoices are settled by a business operation without calling a payment provider. Provider events verify account, identity, amount and currency. A redirect or timeout never establishes settlement. Unknown capability implementations fail deployment; their names do not authorize imagined code generation.

## 9. Browser presentation

Then declares pages using a fixed PatternFly HTML/CSS foundation. App authors choose data, labels, grouping, and actions. No arbitrary HTML, CSS classes, JavaScript, React imports, or `hx-*` attributes. `theme mode=system accent=blue density=comfortable` is shared context; modes are system/light/dark, accents blue/green/purple, density comfortable/compact. These are finite theme tokens, not stylesheets. Component asset acquisition and pruning remain implementation choices.

| Primitive | Supported v1 behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `page /path title="..."` | Shared shell, navigation, title, attached `#` supporting text |
| `card "Heading" [layout=stack\|columns]` | Scope-transparent grouping; columns collapse responsively |
| `title "..."`, `text expr`, `content expr` | Escaped typed content; content preserves plain-text paragraphs, not raw HTML |
| `nav` with `link "Label" to=/path` children | Explicit shared navigation when declared at Then level |
| `list Query`, `table Query columns=...` | Bounded records, selectors, search/filter toolbar, pagination |
| `board Query by=enumField` | Enum-grouped cards with normal actions; no drag/drop |
| `calendar Query start=field end=field` | Date-grouped agenda in the team timezone; no drag/resize |
| `metrics expr,...` | Labeled typed scalar values, not a chart engine |
| `form operation [arguments={...}]` | Generated typed input form; drawer by default, `display=inline` optional |
| `edit [fields=...]`, `delete` | Bound canonical update/delete controls; no duplicate operations |
| `action operation`, `actions operation,...` | Bind existing operations; missing required inputs open their generated form |
| `copy expr`, `details "Heading"` | Clipboard control; expandable content |
| `history` | Authorized, bounded audit entries for the bound row |

There is one page for each normalized route shape. Static segments win only when non-overlapping; `/x/{A.id}` and `/x/{B.id}` conflict. A dynamic record segment is `/invoices/{Invoice.id}` and binds `row:Invoice` after authorized lookup, including its parent chain. Subsequent operations use `row`, not `Invoice` as an instance. Optional path segments and untyped `{id}` are errors. For token/scalar routes, `page /redeem/{token:text} data=redeem(token=token)` invokes a declared pure read operation; the token has no privilege beyond that operation's explicit rule. Page GET is side-effect-free. Team-scoped routes require a selected team; public record routes resolve their team from the record and still enforce policy.

Pages inherit authentication/team requirements from the data they render; `require predicate` in a page can narrow access. Generated team/auth controls live in the shell. Navigation includes accessible static routes by default and never grants access by visibility. Rendered URLs use typed record IDs and escaped values.

A collection child binds `row` and retains its enclosing record chain. An explicit query alias such as `list Invoice as invoice` also remains visible to descendants, so nested forms can name an enclosing record despite row shadowing. A nested direct-child collection automatically scopes to the enclosing parent; unrelated relationships require a `where` query. Bare UI field selectors resolve to that row's schema. A form auto-binds a record parameter only when exactly one compatible record exists in the enclosing chain. Otherwise `arguments={parameter=expr}` is required. Other inputs become controls. Record/member/user pickers use bounded authorized lookup results with safe labels. A user parameter never grants a global account/email directory; without a directory grant it accepts an opaque reference without disclosing account details. `fields` can omit only bound, defaulted, or optional inputs. Server-owned fields never become editable.

Read-form children render its typed `result`; siblings have no result scope. A page `data=` read operation supplies page-level `result`. Mutations re-run authorized page read regions. Preserve unrelated unsaved controls and focus. Validation keeps submitted values; a version conflict presents current authorized values without overwriting them. Expired authentication causes full navigation. Full page GET remains valid; HTMX handles fragments. Runtime must explicitly configure fragment swapping for validation/error statuses because [HTMX does not swap most error responses by default](https://htmx.org/docs/#response-handling).

Collections default to 25 rows, max 100, with identity/team/query-bound opaque cursors. Search is literal text over declared readable fields; filters are typed equality/range/enum inputs, not arbitrary client predicates. `order`, `search`, `filter`, `columns`, `empty`, and form `submit` are supported attributes. A page has a shared maximum of 500 rendered records and 1 MiB of response content; nested sections paginate/lazy-load rather than silently disappear. Runtime limits produce explicit errors where no partial display is meaningful. Query indexes derive from static query shapes and appear in generated migrations.

Shared loading, empty, no-match, validation, failure, and conflict states are mandatory. Strings are escaped; enums and booleans have text-bearing labels; files use authorized links. History requires current record access and projects every entry through current readable-field grants, excluding hidden before/after values and all secrets. Keyboard behavior, focus trapping/return for drawers, field errors, responsive layout, and accessible names belong to runtime. [PatternFly HTML/CSS](https://www.patternfly.org/get-started/develop/) supplies markup/styles; it does not supply every business interaction. Charts, arbitrary rich text, editable opaque JSON, SDK setup widgets, and unconstrained visual editors are outside this v1 catalog.

## 10. MCP and generated interfaces

Every app provides one Streamable HTTP `/mcp` server. Packages contribute namespaced tools, not servers. The compiler emits one operation registry used by UI, MCP, generated routes, and internal calls. Its business tools include model read/list, enabled CRUD, and user scenarios. With teams enabled, owner-authorized `system.team.invite(email,role)`, `.remove(member)`, and `.role(member,role)` are also business tools with the same generated UI rules and mutation envelopes. Their fixed schemas come from the teams primitive. Login, recovery, session management, OAuth consent, source changes, and deployment stay browser/runtime interfaces and are never business tools. Hooks, timers, queues, instrumentation, provider events, and other trusted handlers are never tools.

MCP OAuth consent binds a connection to one app user and one team, or app-only context for a non-team app. Recheck current permissions for discovery and every call; another team requires a separate/re-authorized connection. Tokens have the correct audience and cannot impersonate a source. OAuth/protected-resource discovery follows the [MCP authorization specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization). Browser sessions and MCP grants resolve the same principal model.

Tool names are stable `package.Model.read`, `.list`, `.create`, `.update`, `.delete`, and `package.scenario`; `main` remains explicit in tool names even when implicit in source. The app description becomes initialization `instructions`; attached operation descriptions become tool descriptions. Model/field descriptions enrich generated schemas. `##` never leaves the source. File moves change no tool name.

Schemas are closed typed JSON objects. Model reference inputs use `{id}` for reads and `{id,version}` for mutations; money uses integer minor units/currency; datetimes use RFC 3339 UTC strings; files use completed opaque IDs; union values have a discriminator. All int/decimal values use canonical decimal strings at the MCP boundary, including money.minor and record.version; there is no magnitude-dependent wire type. Booleans and collection counts defined by the protocol itself remain JSON booleans/numbers. Mutations have an `operation_id`; identity, roles, and team grants cannot be arguments. Generated CRUD update takes `{record,changes,operation_id}`; scenario business inputs are named alongside `operation_id`. Unknown arguments and undeclared writable fields fail.

Model list tools accept typed filters/order/cursor/limit constrained by readable fields, and a parent reference for children. Results reuse the UI query and projection rules. Every mutation result has `{status,operation_id,records,deliveries,result}` with applicable members present; pure reads return their declared shape. Business errors use structured codes (`validation`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `rule_failed`, `busy`, `limit`, `delivery_unknown`) and actionable safe details with `isError=true`. Existence-hiding lookups return `not_found`. Protocol errors remain JSON-RPC errors. These choices follow [MCP tools/schema boundaries](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools), not an additional app API definition.

## 11. Compiler output and change ownership

Compilation parses and type-checks, resolves names/ownership/permissions/effects, and emits one workerd application, generated interfaces, Cloudflare binding requirements, and versioned schema/index migrations. These are compiler phases, not app framework layers. Diagnostics identify file/declaration/field and one concrete error; unknown syntax is an error, not an AI interpretation opportunity.

Application source has no executable general-purpose escape hatch. Pure derivations compose expressions; scenarios compose canonical effects; integrations implement declared external contracts. The compiler does not invent business decisions, provider mappings, field names, or functions to make a source file appear complete.

Compatible automatic migrations add models, optional/defaulted fields, and indexes. Renames/removals, required backfills, enum removal, owner changes, and semantic transformations require an explicit versioned migration. Never infer a rename from similar spelling or erase data to satisfy a compile. Pending work keeps its release/declaration contract; deployment must migrate, drain, or explicitly invalidate incompatible jobs before replacing that handler. Schema migration is maintenance behavior, never an MCP business tool. Generated Cloudflare deployment configuration tracks its supported provider version; application data migrations are distinct from Durable Object class lifecycle configuration.

The language version pins builtin signatures, wire schemas, currency scales, timezone data, runtime defaults, and component behavior. App deployments record that version without repeating a version on every declaration. Compiler/runtime versions cannot silently reinterpret a running app. Component download/tree-shaking, SQL planning, password-hash implementation, and bundler choice are implementation work; their absence is not permission to invent alternative source syntax.

## 12. What is complete, and what remains

This freezes a bounded v1 design: composition, descriptions, type/scoping rules, a closed expression/effect vocabulary, permissions, CRUD, trusted events, transactions, integrations, UI, and MCP. It deliberately replaces ambiguous draft forms; it is not a backwards-compatibility promise to sketches. Cross-service atomicity, arbitrary runtime code, destructive automatic migrations, general-purpose visual editing, and claims of complete support for every historical draft are explicitly excluded.

[examples/TeamTasks.can](examples/TeamTasks.can) and [examples/ExpenseFlow.can](examples/ExpenseFlow.can) are manually checked reference source for this design. The 35 files in `draft/` remain application-design evidence and need migration before they can be v1 fixtures. Their prose operations must be implemented with these defined primitives or expose a concrete missing feature. Unsupported app foundations cannot enlarge v1 by implication.

Implementation remains: parser/type checker, operation runtime, Cloudflare deployment adapter, UI/MCP generation, and executable validation against the app requirements. The first material runtime uncertainty is D1 fence contention under representative workloads. No compiler, successful app execution, production security review, or performance result is claimed by this design work.
files.examples/TeamTasks.can:
# Manage team tasks, assign active teammates, and track completion.
app TeamTasks
Given
  runtime workerd
  database D1
  auth email password
  teams
  Todo in team { title:text! trim max=200, done:bool=false, assignee:member? }
  policy Todo read=members
When
  crud Todo by=members fields=title,done,assignee
Then
  # Add work, assign teammates, and track what is finished.
  page / title="Team tasks"
    form Todo.create fields=title,assignee submit="Add task" display=inline
    list Todo order=-created search=title filter=done empty="No tasks yet. Add your first task."
      edit
      delete
files.examples/ExpenseFlow.can:
# Submit team expenses and let a reviewer approve or reject them.
app ExpenseFlow
context
  runtime workerd
  database D1
  auth email password
  teams

package expenses
  Given
    role reviewer in=team
    Expense in team {
      purpose:text! trim max=300,
      amount:money!,
      submitted_by:user server=actor,
      status:enum(draft,submitted,approved,rejected)=draft,
      decision_note:text?,
      decided_by:user?,
      decided_at:datetime?
    }
    policy Expense read=members where=row.submitted_by==actor
    policy Expense read=reviewer
    require Expense: row.amount.minor>0
    lock Expense fields=purpose,amount,submitted_by when=row.status!=draft
    lock Expense fields=status,decision_note,decided_by,decided_at when=row.status in [approved,rejected]
  When
    crud Expense by=members fields=purpose,amount when=row.submitted_by==actor and row.status==draft delete=none
    # Submit your own draft expense for review.
    scenario submit(expense:Expense) by=members
      require expense.submitted_by==actor and expense.status==draft
      then set expense {status=submitted}
    # Approve a submitted expense from another teammate, optionally recording a note.
    scenario approve(expense:Expense,note:text?) by=reviewer
      require expense.status==submitted and expense.submitted_by!=actor
      then set expense {status=approved,decision_note=note,decided_by=actor,decided_at=now}
    # Reject a submitted expense from another teammate and explain the decision.
    scenario reject(expense:Expense,note:text) by=reviewer
      require expense.status==submitted and expense.submitted_by!=actor and trim(note)!=""
      then set expense {status=rejected,decision_note=note,decided_by=actor,decided_at=now}
  Then
    # Prepare expenses and follow their review status.
    page / title="Expenses"
      form Expense.create
      list Expense order=-created filter=status
        edit
        actions submit,approve,reject
        history

package reporting
  use expenses.Expense
  Given
    contract Summary { count:int!, total:money! }
  When
    # Summarize expenses you can read, in one currency and status.
    scenario summarize(currency:currency,status:Expense.status) read=true -> Summary by=members
      then
        let selected=Expense as expense where expense.amount.currency==currency and expense.status==status
        return Summary {count=count(selected),total=sum(selected as expense select expense.amount,currency)}
  Then
    # Choose a currency and status to total the expenses visible to you.
    page /reports title="Expense summary"
      form summarize display=inline
        metrics result.count,result.total

criteria.coherent: These design rules are mutually consistent for this property.
